title: CTF-5: Defend
intro: Every unlock here is *retrospective* — something the student (or the attacker bot) already did, never a pointer to where the bug is. That's deliberate: the lab's only hint mechanism is the SOC Alerts panel's own pattern (recon, then probes, then the real payload), and nothing in this catalog may spell out the flaw or the fix (see ROADMAP.md's achievements-design note). Triggers here: `soc:` (the attacker-bot swarm's own traffic against the student's `customer-portal` slot — `recon`, `probe`, `exploit_attempt`, `contained`), `ctf:` (`dump_success`, the bot's own successful exfiltration), `forgejo:` (the student's PR against their own `{user}/customer-portal` repo). Milestones are the green, 'you did something' track; funny unlocks are the red, 'something happened to you' track — neither carries real points pressure (funny is always 0; milestones use the house default, kept small on purpose, since CTF-5 is a cooperative incident, not a leaderboard race). Scoring: `d-patched` and `d-unbreached` are worth one unit each (green is both, yellow is `d-patched` alone, red neither), at the factor `CTF_SCORE_FACTOR` (workshop.env, default 5 points per unit). Three targets are live per student (`customer-portal`, `policy-bypass`, `leaky-config`); soc/ctf triggers are matched on the event's `challenge` (the target name) and forgejo triggers on the student's own repo of that name. Ids without a suffix are `customer-portal`'s (kept stable); `-pb` and `-lc` are `policy-bypass` and `leaky-config`. Scoring weights (3 / 2 / 1) are applied by the SOC scoring, not here.
